patches.reason: A match holds its die value, or the text X once it is matched, so the round totals add values that may be text; TeaseScript + adds numbers or joins texts, not both. The totals are taken right after both sides rolled, when every match is a number, so each value goes through toInteger().

Four Heroes pays a lost game out with for(i in 0..2) over its two implements, [lightImplement, heavyImplement], so a third round told the player to grab "null" and repeated the heavy implement's swats (Groovy read null past the end; TeaseScript stops the script there). Its siblings loop over exactly their lists, Rock Paper Scissors 0..2 over three implements and Hit or Stay 0..3 over four: loop 0..1. The corpus's other loops over a constant range stay within the lists they index.

Hit or Stay reads and saves whether the player already met an opponent under Banjo.fourheroes.played_<opponent>, Four Heroes' key, while its own reset clears Banjo.hitorstay.played_<opponent> and every other game uses its own prefix: so a Four Heroes game made Hit or Stay greet the opponent as met before, and Hit or Stay's reset never cleared it. Use Banjo.hitorstay.played_.

Penalty Box's three-player finale has a result for every order of the scores except the two AI opponents tying above the player, which left winner and loser null: the host announced a winner "null" and nobody was spanked. Add that case as its sibling ties have it: a draw, with the player the loser.

Four Heroes, Game of Chance and Guess the Number list the light implement toys.bat_battledore, which nothing saves: the implements form, these games' own cases for the battledore bat, and the other games all use toys.bat_jokari. So an owned battledore bat was never picked in these three games. List toys.bat_jokari.
